doc.what: Close the two gaps the gh #80 re-measure found in readable-content's delivered work: the readability check calls three kinds of unreadable extraction readable, and the Reddit fetcher never fetches the article behind a link post that carries any self-text.
doc.why: Re-measured on cerebro 2026-10-03 for items created since the readable-content deploy (2026-09-30), content under 300 chars: youtube 0/21 (was 56/126), reddit 5/160 (was 270/1594), rss 17/217 (was 154/1720). The RSS share barely moved. 14 of the 17 are Hacker News `Comments` stubs correctly marked title_only (paywalls, PDFs, empty extractions). The other 3 are marked readable and reach analysis as content: trafilatura returned 'This page needs JavaScript.' plus loading text (stoppels.ch), the two glyphs '‹ ›' (frogandtoad.ai), and YouTube's footer navigation (an HN link to youtube.com). `is_readable` in readability.py matches one literal React noscript sentence and only tag-only text, so each new wording of the same failure passes. Separately, 8 of 37 external Reddit link posts since the deploy hold no article text: `_to_content_item` in fetchers/reddit.py appends the post's self-text instead of calling `extract_article` whenever self-text exists, so a link post with a two-line note never gets its article, although trafilatura extracts 23,970 and 13,192 chars from two of those links (ifritnoises.org, binsec.no) today.
decided: The readability check stays shape-based with no bare length floor; one-sentence news blurbs and two-line Reddit questions stay readable (readable-content SC-1).
JavaScript-walled pages are title-only, not rendered (readable-content out of scope).
The fix lives in the one check in readability.py that every consumer already calls; no second check is added.

A Reddit link post to an external article gets the article text alongside the link and any self-text, through the shared `extract_article`; image, video and reddit-internal links stay as they are; a failed extraction keeps today's content.
Items already stored and analysed are not reclassified or re-fetched; a backfill stays a separate, costed decision.
Routing an HN link to youtube.com through the YouTube transcript fetcher stays out of scope (readable-content out of scope: no different route for HN's linked article).
open: How does the check recognize a JavaScript-required notice beyond the one literal React sentence, so wordings like 'This page needs JavaScript.' are caught, without calling an article that discusses JavaScript unreadable?

What shape test replaces the markup-only check so text with no sentence in it at all (site navigation and footer chrome, lone glyphs) is not readable, while a one-sentence blurb and a two-line question stay readable?
